data.text/markdown:
CRISPRi HLC Trial3 D28 (fixed) -- B2M knockdown analysis

This notebook measures B2M knockdown efficiency across three independent arms in fixed cells from HLC Trial 3, Day 28, each arm using a different guide-delivery method and/or cell line. It parses the raw flow cytometry (FCS) files for each well, applies cell and antibody gates, and reports the percentage-point shift in the fraction of cells below a fixed B2M-antibody gate, comparing a non-targeting control guide (NT-GFP) to the B2M-targeting guide (B2M-GFP), within cells confirmed to carry the guide and/or effector virus. This dataset targets the B2M gene and includes no CD81 antibody stain. Two well groups are excluded from the knockdown analysis: wells from the K562 cell line, used only to check ASGR1-antibody specificity, and two guide-only wells with no effector virus, used only as GFP compensation controls.

data.text/html: Experimental arms at a glance

Plot 1. Knockdown across all 3 arms Why: This plot answers which of the 3 knockdown arms shows the largest B2M knockdown, and whether the answer depends on which of the two knockdown metrics is used.
How: For each arm, the primary guide-active (B2M-GFP) group's % of cells below a gate is compared to that same arm's own mock/control group, at two gates: the 1st-percentile-of-mock gate (tail effect) and the 50th-percentile-of-mock gate (population-level shift). The difference (guide-active minus control, in percentage points) is the knockdown number plotted here. How to read it: Each arm is one group of two bars: red is the 1st-percentile-of-mock knockdown, purple is the 50th-percentile-of-mock knockdown, both in percentage points. See each arm's own tab below for full per-replicate detail, ASGR1+ stratification, and caveats.
Result: The largest 1st-percentile knockdown is 15.7pp, in the "17_3 stably-integrated guide + AA239 effector (two-component)" arm; the largest 50th-percentile knockdown is 29.1pp, in the "17_3 stably-integrated guide + AA239 effector (two-component)" arm.

data.text/markdown:
How to read each panel below

Each tab is one construct/cell-line arm: a short description of the delivery biology, well metadata, a peak-normalized histogram + FlowJo-style scatter of the B2M readout channel (gated on guide/effector-delivery markers, dashed red line = 1st-percentile-of-mock gate, dashed purple line = 50th-percentile-of-mock gate), a per-replicate bar chart for each metric, and a tidy summary table. Nested "All cells"/"ASGR1+" sub-tabs stratify by ASGR1-BV421 where available. Every plot in this notebook is numbered (Plot 1, Plot 2, ...) and preceded by a short Why/How/How-to-read-it note, with a Result line stating the computed numbers after the plot. Numbers follow each plot's position in the notebook's cell order, not the order tabs happen to be clicked in, so a number may appear out of visual sequence when viewed inside a nested tab.

Plot 30. WTC11 transient B2M-GFP virus: knockdown across strata Why: This plot states whether selecting for the ASGR1+ cell group changes the measured knockdown for WTC11 transient B2M-GFP virus, compared to using all gated cells regardless of ASGR1 status.
How: The 1st- and 50th-percentile-of-mock knockdown (pp) for the B2M-GFP (guide), +dox group is computed twice: once over all gated cells, once restricted to the ASGR1+ stratum, then plotted side by side. How to read it: Each pair of bars is one cell group (all cells, or ASGR1+); red bars are the 1st-percentile-of-mock metric, purple bars are the 50th-percentile-of-mock metric, both in percentage points of knockdown.
TL;DR: ASGR1+ selection lowers 1st-percentile knockdown (5.8pp -> 1.0pp, -4.8pp) and raises the 50th-percentile metric (3.4pp -> 5.5pp, +2.1pp).ASGR1-BV421 (co-stained in-well) is the only hepatocyte marker available for stratification in this dataset. Albumin is stained only on separate, non-arm reference wells (see the informational hepatocyte-marker section above).
Construct: NT-GFP (non-targeting guide, GFP-marked) vs B2M-GFP (B2M-targeting guide, GFP-marked) delivered as a single transient virus into WTC11 cells. WTC11 carries a doxycycline-inducible CRISPRi effector, so the B2M-GFP group is split into no dox (effector off, expected to show no knockdown) and +dox (effector on, expected to show knockdown) -- this induction status is this arm's main experimental variable, so these wells are kept as separate groups rather than averaged together. GFP+ = confirmed transduction. Readout: B2M-APC.
Plot 42. Arm 1 (WTC11 transient B2M-GFP virus): GFP (guide) (FITC-A) infection-marker distribution Why: States whether cells in Arm 1 (WTC11 transient B2M-GFP virus) were successfully transduced/marked for GFP (guide), the gate that feeds this arm's knockdown analysis.
How: FITC-A values (debris/doublet/singlet-gated, compensated) are pooled across replicate wells within each condition group and plotted as peak-normalized histograms, with an unstained or FMO reference overlaid. How to read it: Same layout as the gate-calibration histograms above: biexponential x-axis, % of each group's peak count on the y-axis, dashed red line is the gate.
Plot 43. Arm 1 (WTC11 transient B2M-GFP virus): GFP (guide) (FITC-A) vs SSC-A Why: Checks the infection-marker-positive population as a distinct group in 2D against granularity (SSC-A).
How: A fixed-seed random subsample of the same gated, compensated events is plotted as a scatter (never pooled across groups). How to read it: Same x-axis as the histogram above; the dashed red line marks the same gate.
Plot 44. Arm 1 (WTC11 transient B2M-GFP virus): % GFP (guide)+ per replicate Why: States the GFP (guide) infection/transduction rate for Arm 1 (WTC11 transient B2M-GFP virus) directly, per replicate well.
How: For each well, % of gated cells above the GFP (guide) gate is computed. How to read it: Each bar is one replicate well; n (gated cell count) is printed above each bar.
Result: Overall GFP (guide)+ rate in Arm 1 (WTC11 transient B2M-GFP virus): 913.3% (n-weighted across replicate wells).

Knockdown: APC-A

Two complementary metrics below: the red 1st-percentile-of-mock gate captures a tail/low-signal effect (cells shifted furthest down); the purple 50th-percentile-of-mock gate captures a broader population-level shift (whether the bulk of the distribution moved, not just the tail).
Plot 14. WTC11 transient B2M-GFP virus -- APC-A distribution Why: This plot answers whether the B2M-GFP (guide), +dox group shows lower APC-A signal than the NT-GFP (control) group in the WTC11 transient B2M-GFP virus arm, which is the basis of the B2M-knockdown measurement for this arm.
How: APC-A values (gated on this arm's guide/effector-delivery markers, and compensated for cross-channel spillover) are pooled across replicate wells within each condition group, then binned into a histogram and normalized so each group's tallest bin reads 100%. An unstained reference well is overlaid for comparison. How to read it: The x-axis is APC-A on a biexponential scale (linear near zero, log-like at high values); the y-axis is % of each group's own peak count, so every group's curve has the same height regardless of cell count. Each line is one condition group, pooled across its replicate wells. The dashed red line is the 1st-percentile-of-NT-GFP (control) gate; the dashed purple line is the 50th-percentile-of-NT-GFP (control) gate.
Result: Averaged across replicate wells, 6.8% of B2M-GFP (guide), +dox cells (n=5,882) fall below the 1st-percentile-of-NT-GFP (control) gate, versus 1.0% of NT-GFP (control) cells (n=5,596) -- a +5.8 percentage-point difference.
Plot 15. WTC11 transient B2M-GFP virus -- APC-A vs SSC-A Why: This plot checks whether the APC-A signal difference between B2M-GFP (guide), +dox and NT-GFP (control) corresponds to a distinct population in 2D (not just a 1D histogram artifact), and lets the gate position be checked against the granularity (SSC-A) axis.
How: The same gated, compensated APC-A values as the histogram above are plotted against each cell's SSC-A, with replicate wells in the same group pooled into one density contour per group (never pooled across groups). How to read it: The x-axis is APC-A (biexponential scale, same as the histogram above); the y-axis is SSC-A, capped at the 99.5th percentile of plotted events so the main population is not compressed by outliers. Each colored contour is one condition group. The dashed red/purple lines mark the same two gates as the histogram above.
Result: The B2M-GFP (guide), +dox and NT-GFP (control) populations are visible as separate density contours along the APC-A axis, consistent with the shift seen in the histogram above.
Plot 16. WTC11 transient B2M-GFP virus -- % below 1st-percentile-of-mock gate Why: This plot states the tail-effect knockdown number for WTC11 transient B2M-GFP virus directly, per replicate well.
How: For each well, the % of gated cells below the 1st-percentile-of-NT-GFP (control) gate (from the histogram above) is computed, then the mean of the NT-GFP (control) wells is subtracted from each well's value to give a knockdown in percentage points (pp). How to read it: Each bar is one replicate well, labeled with its condition and well ID; the bar height is % of cells below the gate, with n (gated cell count) printed above each bar.
Result: Mean knockdown for B2M-GFP (guide), +dox vs. NT-GFP (control) at this gate is +5.8 percentage points, averaged across 2 replicate well(s).
Plot 17. WTC11 transient B2M-GFP virus -- % below 50th-percentile-of-mock gate Why: This plot states the population-level-shift knockdown number for WTC11 transient B2M-GFP virus directly, per replicate well.
How: Same computation as the previous plot, using the 50th-percentile-of-NT-GFP (control) gate instead of the 1st percentile, so it captures a shift of the bulk of the distribution rather than only the lowest-signal tail. How to read it: Same layout as the previous bar chart, at the 50th-percentile gate.
Result: Mean knockdown for B2M-GFP (guide), +dox vs. NT-GFP (control) at this gate is +3.4 percentage points, averaged across 2 replicate well(s).
Plot 26. WTC11 transient B2M-GFP virus -- ASGR1+: APC-A distribution Why: This plot checks whether the B2M-GFP (guide), +dox vs. NT-GFP (control) knockdown signal seen across all cells in WTC11 transient B2M-GFP virus still holds within the ASGR1+ cell group specifically.
How: Same computation as the arm's unstratified histogram (pooled across replicate wells within each condition group), but restricted to cells additionally passing the ASGR1+ marker gate. How to read it: Same layout as the unstratified histogram: biexponential x-axis, % of each well's peak count on the y-axis, dashed red/purple lines mark the 1st- and 50th-percentile-of-mock gates for this stratum.
Plot 27. WTC11 transient B2M-GFP virus -- ASGR1+: APC-A vs SSC-A Why: This plot checks the ASGR1+ population separation in 2D, the same purpose as the arm's unstratified scatter plot.
How: Same computation as the arm's unstratified scatter plot, restricted to this stratum. How to read it: Same layout as the unstratified scatter plot above.
Plot 28. WTC11 transient B2M-GFP virus -- ASGR1+: % below 1st-percentile-of-mock gate Why: States the tail-effect knockdown number for the ASGR1+ stratum directly, per replicate well.
How: Same computation as the arm's unstratified 1st-percentile bar chart, restricted to this stratum. How to read it: Same layout as the arm's unstratified bar chart.
Result: Mean knockdown for B2M-GFP (guide), +dox vs. NT-GFP (control) within the ASGR1+ stratum is +1.0 percentage points (n=2,416 B2M-GFP (guide), +dox cells).
Plot 29. WTC11 transient B2M-GFP virus -- ASGR1+: % below 50th-percentile-of-mock gate Why: States the population-level-shift knockdown number for the ASGR1+ stratum directly, per replicate well.
How: Same computation as the arm's unstratified 50th-percentile bar chart, restricted to this stratum. How to read it: Same layout as the arm's unstratified bar chart.
Result: Mean knockdown for B2M-GFP (guide), +dox vs. NT-GFP (control) within the ASGR1+ stratum is +5.5 percentage points (n=2,416 B2M-GFP (guide), +dox cells).

Arm 2 infection-gating: transduction-reagent comparison

Arm 2's 12 wells compare 3 lentiviral delivery reagents for the AA239 effector virus (Transduction Reagent column in the sample sheet): Polybrene (C1-C4), Protamine Sulfate (C5-C8), Lentiboost (D1-D4) -- 4 wells each (2 NT-GFP + 2 B2M-GFP).
Plot 9. Arm 2 transduction-reagent comparison Why: This plot answers which of the 3 transduction reagents delivers the AA239 effector virus most efficiently in Arm 2.
How: For each well, % Thy1.1-APC+ (confirmed effector delivery) is computed using the Thy1.1-APC effector-delivery gate slider above, then grouped by reagent. How to read it: Each bar is one well, labeled by reagent, guide condition, and replicate number (e.g. "PB: NT-GFP rep1"); n (gated cell count) is printed above each bar. Wells are grouped into 3 reagent blocks (dotted vertical lines mark the boundaries) -- "rep1"/"rep2" under different reagents are different physical wells, not matched replicates of each other, so bars are not meant to be compared left-to-right across reagent blocks by replicate number, only by reagent-level means (see Result below).
Result: Mean % Thy1.1-APC+ by reagent: Lentiboost 80.7%, Polybrene 82.6%, Protamine Sulfate 82.8%. Protamine Sulfate gives the highest mean effector-delivery rate.

Knockdown: B610-ECD-A

Two complementary metrics below: the red 1st-percentile-of-mock gate captures a tail/low-signal effect (cells shifted furthest down); the purple 50th-percentile-of-mock gate captures a broader population-level shift (whether the bulk of the distribution moved, not just the tail).
Plot 22. 17_3 fully-transient two-virus (guide + AA239 effector) -- B610-ECD-A distribution Why: This plot answers whether the B2M-GFP (guide) group shows lower B610-ECD-A signal than the NT-GFP (control) group in the 17_3 fully-transient two-virus (guide + AA239 effector) arm, which is the basis of the B2M-knockdown measurement for this arm.
How: B610-ECD-A values (gated on this arm's guide/effector-delivery markers, and compensated for cross-channel spillover) are pooled across replicate wells within each condition group, then binned into a histogram and normalized so each group's tallest bin reads 100%. An unstained reference well is overlaid for comparison. How to read it: The x-axis is B610-ECD-A on a biexponential scale (linear near zero, log-like at high values); the y-axis is % of each group's own peak count, so every group's curve has the same height regardless of cell count. Each line is one condition group, pooled across its replicate wells. The dashed red line is the 1st-percentile-of-NT-GFP (control) gate; the dashed purple line is the 50th-percentile-of-NT-GFP (control) gate.
Result: Averaged across replicate wells, 7.7% of B2M-GFP (guide) cells (n=6,896) fall below the 1st-percentile-of-NT-GFP (control) gate, versus 1.1% of NT-GFP (control) cells (n=8,540) -- a +6.6 percentage-point difference.

How: The same gated, compensated B610-ECD-A values as the histogram above are plotted against each cell's SSC-A, with replicate wells in the same group pooled into one density contour per group (never pooled across groups). How to read it: The x-axis is B610-ECD-A (biexponential scale, same as the histogram above); the y-axis is SSC-A, capped at the 99.5th percentile of plotted events so the main population is not compressed by outliers. Each colored contour is one condition group. The dashed red/purple lines mark the same two gates as the histogram above.
Result: The B2M-GFP (guide) and NT-GFP (control) populations are visible as separate density contours along the B610-ECD-A axis, consistent with the shift seen in the histogram above.
Plot 24. 17_3 fully-transient two-virus (guide + AA239 effector) -- % below 1st-percentile-of-mock gate Why: This plot states the tail-effect knockdown number for 17_3 fully-transient two-virus (guide + AA239 effector) directly, per replicate well.

How to read it: Each bar is one replicate well, labeled with its condition and well ID; the bar height is % of cells below the gate, with n (gated cell count) printed above each bar.
